options.text: Studying the structure of DNA
The direct manipulation of an organism's DNA to alter its characteristics
Selectively breeding organisms over many generations
Cloning organisms to produce identical copies

questions.explanation: Genetic engineering is the direct manipulation of an organism's DNA by inserting genes from another organism. Unlike selective breeding, it can transfer specific genes between different species in a single generation.

questions.stem: What is the role of restriction enzymes in genetic engineering?

options.text: To translate DNA into protein
To join pieces of DNA together
To cut DNA at specific recognition sites
To copy DNA during replication

questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific base sequences (recognition sites). They are used to cut out the desired gene from the source organism's DNA and to open up the vector DNA so the gene can be inserted.

questions.stem: What is a vector in genetic engineering?

options.text: The enzyme that cuts DNA
The protein produced by the inserted gene
The organism that donates the gene
A carrier used to transfer a gene into the target organism

questions.explanation: A vector is a carrier molecule used to transfer the desired gene into the target organism. Common vectors include bacterial plasmids and viruses. The gene is inserted into the vector, which then delivers it to the target cell.

questions.stem: Which enzyme is used to join the desired gene into the vector DNA?

options.text: Restriction enzyme
RNA polymerase
DNA polymerase
DNA ligase

questions.explanation: DNA ligase joins the desired gene into the vector DNA by forming bonds between the sugar-phosphate backbones. It 'glues' the gene into the vector, creating recombinant DNA.

questions.stem: An important medical application of genetic engineering is the production of:

options.text: Antibiotics
Human insulin by genetically modified bacteria
Vaccines using selective breeding
X-ray machines

questions.explanation: Genetically modified bacteria are used to produce human insulin for treating diabetes. The human insulin gene is inserted into bacteria, which then produce large quantities of human insulin that is identical to the natural form.

questions.stem: What is a potential concern about genetically modified (GM) crops?

options.text: They require more water than normal crops
They always taste worse than normal crops
Modified genes could transfer to wild plant populations
They cannot grow in soil

questions.explanation: One concern about GM crops is that modified genes could transfer to wild plant populations through cross-pollination. For example, herbicide resistance genes could spread to weeds, creating 'superweeds' that are difficult to control.

options.text: An organism produced by selective breeding
An organism that contains genes from a different species
An organism that has been cloned
An organism that has undergone natural selection

questions.explanation: A transgenic organism contains genes from a different species that have been inserted through genetic engineering. For example, bacteria containing the human insulin gene are transgenic organisms.
